rationale: B wins because it makes the load-bearing proof explicit before the founder walks into a reporter's first hard question: "which leg of the transfer the stablecoin actually replaces" and "a concrete settlement-time and cost comparison versus correspondent banking on at least one named corridor." A is strong, but "For a profitable public payments company, cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story" drifts into investor math the supplied facts do not yet earn. Both avoid most crypto victory-lap nonsense; B is simply tighter and more useful under pressure.
gaps_in_A: "For a profitable public payments company, cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story" assumes Wise's own margin benefit from facts that only say businesses can move money faster and cheaper.
"confirmation of the specific stablecoin and regulatory partner" invents a "regulatory partner"; the update says the stablecoin and partner are unnamed, not that a regulatory partner exists.
"with the correspondent-banking system as the protagonist under threat" overcooks the threat without corridor data, adoption share, or proof that Wise is displacing a meaningful bank leg.
The payments-infrastructure angle needs the mechanics B asks for: which leg the stablecoin replaces, not just a generic comment from SWIFT or a bank analyst.
gaps_in_B: "skipping correspondent banks" is a hair too declarative until Wise proves which settlement leg the stablecoin actually replaces.
"the trend a market's edge case becomes its plumbing" is a tortured headline and too sweeping unless the independent institutional-adoption context materializes.
"stablecoin regulation is actively being set" imports an outside news peg not supplied in the update; the region-by-region approval fact is enough.
It leaves a plausible equities/unit-economics path on the table: publicly listed, profitable, £30B per quarter is a markets hook, though it would need hard cost-disclosure proof.
